headline: High: Roo Code’s default workspace write/network/MCP capabilities can leak or corrupt shared files when paired with Pathway’s document-processing pipeline; prompt-injection risk is lower but still present via shared workspace content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pathway is document-processing with no filesystem read/write or clipboard surfaces, so it is not itself a bridge. Roo Code reads and writes VS Code workspace files and can use MCP, so if Pathway outputs land in a shared workspace, Roo can ingest attacker-controlled content as instructions. The pathway is interaction-based, not provably blocked.
conditions: IF Pathway outputs are written into a workspace file that Roo Code opens or parses
IF Roo Code is configured to treat workspace content as instructions or tool input
mitigations: Separate Pathway outputs from Roo Code workspaces
Disable MCP servers not needed for the task
Use a read-only handoff file for Pathway outputs
Add a manual review step before Roo Code consumes generated text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Pathway touches no data classes in the profile, but Roo Code handles source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys while having broad network egress and filesystem access. If both share a workspace, Roo can transmit file contents to configured APIs, creating a plausible leakage path from shared artifacts even though Pathway itself is not shown to upload data.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared VS Code workspace
IF Roo Code sends workspace content to a configured model API or MCP server
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Restrict Roo Code to non-sensitive folders
Rotate or scope API keys used by Roo Code
Disable browser/screenshot workflows for sensitive tasks
Use separate OS users or containers for the two agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Pathway has no write or network capabilities, but Roo Code has unrestricted filesystem write, modify_git_state, and broad network egress with shared-state-via-filesystem concurrency. If both operate on the same workspace or repo, Roo can overwrite or race with Pathway-produced artifacts; uncertainty is limited because Roo’s write surface is explicit and Pathway’s lack of writes does not prevent conflict.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or git repository
IF Roo Code performs edits while Pathway is generating or transforming files
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git branches per agent
Enable file locking in the orchestrator
Review diffs before any commit

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pathway can generate transformed documents or pipeline outputs, and Roo Code can act on workspace content with terminal and browser tools. If Roo treats Pathway output as authoritative, errors can cascade into edits, commits, or external actions. Pathway is not documented as verifying Roo’s downstream actions, so the interaction is plausible and not safely bounded.
conditions: IF Roo Code consumes Pathway output without an explicit verification step
IF Roo Code uses that output to edit files, browse, or commit changes
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require human approval before commits or external actions
Have Roo Code cite source files before acting
Limit Roo Code to read-only review mode for Pathway outputs

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for Pathway, while Roo Code explicitly handles model-provider API keys and can send data to configured APIs. Because the profiles do not specify regulated data classes or a cross-border policy conflict, only a low compliance risk is supportable from the documented surfaces.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Roo Code prompts or workspace files
IF the configured model API or MCP server has retention or residency terms that differ from the operator's policy
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in prompts
Review provider retention settings
Use a region-approved API endpoint
Document the data flow before enabling MCP
Keep API keys in a separate secret store
